<h2>One hectare, many promises</h2>
<p>Climate, biodiversity, energy, housing and food are all asking more of the same land. The farmer who lives from it is rarely at the table.</p>

<h3>We cannot drink gold</h3>
<p>Ghana arrests hundreds of illegal miners a year and convicts a handful. The deeper problem is who profits from the gold and who pays for the water.</p>

<span class="feature-kicker">Policy</span>
<h3>Thirty years of Irish tree-planting promises, checked against the record</h3>
<p>Ireland has planted a fraction of the forest it promised since 1996. Licensing explains one bad stretch. Farmers walking away from planting explains more of the gap.</p>

<h2>About my research</h2>

<p class="home-statement">My research examines how national agricultural, climate and land-use goals translate into different costs, opportunities and constraints across farms and places. I work with spatial, economic and behavioural models at the University of Galway.</p>
